relations.note: Clerical traditions substitute Diana and Holda as leaders of nocturnal companies.

relations.myth: Leadership of the nocturnal spirit company
relations.note: Canonistic and demonological traditions place Herodias and Holda within the same night-leader naming complex.
Sources equate or correlate them as regional forms sharing winter, spinning, reward, and punishment functions.
Lady Holda is called Queen of Heaven, possibly reflecting Marian syncretism or clerical interpretation.

relations.myth: Learned comparison of household and spinning functions
relations.note: Grimm and later scholars proposed identity from shared functions and suggestive northern regional names.
Modern scholarship proposes Freyja as an ancestral or cognate figure without primary-text interaction.

relations.myth: Comparison through underworld and death-related traits
relations.note: Modern writers equate them through names and underworld traits, though no medieval source does.

relations.myth: Comparison through fertility and earth functions
relations.note: Modern comparison links their fertility and seasonal associations without a connecting textual tradition.
Antiquarian and philological conjecture identifies inscribed Hludana as Holda's predecessor, but the equation remains unproven.

relations.myth: Parallel leadership of the Wild Hunt
relations.note: Grimm compared Holle's furious host with Wodan's; no meeting or joint ride is attested.
